newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Litrak debuts at 5.60 rgt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Litrak debuts at 5.60 rgt.

text.p: Shares of Lingkaran Trans Kota Holdings Bhd (Litrak) debuted on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) on Thursday at 5.60 ringgit.
The company had offered 18.78 million shares to the Malaysian public at 3.60 ringgit per share, and 55 million shares to institutional investors at 5.10 ringgit each.
The infrastructure company is listed on the KLSE's Main Board.

Litrak is the second company listed under the Securities Commission's new guidelines on lisiting on infrastructure project companies after Powertek Bhd. Litrak holds a concession to construct and operate a 40-km toll road for 33 years.
Analysts said upside for the stock appears limited as earnings would only start to come in by the year 2000.
"Judging by our estimates on traffic growth which were very conservative, Litrak is in for quite a big earnings surprise come the year 2000," Jupiter Securities said in a report to clients.
"But why buy now, because it would be difficult for the stock to rise sharply," it said.
